---
title: "Hydra basics"
---

Hydra lets you choose a dataset, model and training settings without editing
Python. METIS includes default configurations in the installed package.

## Start from the defaults

```bash
uv run metis train --cfg job
```

This prints the configuration without training. Its main groups are `dataset`,
`model` and `training`. Each group is a small YAML file; Hydra combines them
into one experiment configuration.

To select the transformer and change the training budget:

```bash
uv run metis train model=transformer training.steps=1000
```

`model=transformer` selects a configuration. `training.steps=1000` overrides a
value inside one. Nested settings use dots in the same way:

```bash
uv run metis train model=mlp model.model_options.hidden_dim=128
```

## What is in a configuration?

For example, the MLP configuration contains:

```yaml
_target_: metis.Surrogate
_convert_: all
model: mlp
observed_outputs: []
model_options:
  hidden_dim: 64
  num_blocks: 2
  num_layers_per_block: 2
```

`_target_` tells Hydra which Python constructor to call. The remaining values
are its arguments; `_convert_: all` converts YAML collections into ordinary
Python lists and dictionaries.

## Try several settings

```bash
uv run metis train --multirun model=mlp,transformer training.learning_rate=0.001,0.0003 evaluation.partition=validation
```

This runs four combinations and saves each run in its own directory. Choose
settings using validation data; keep the test data for the final evaluation.

For your own bank, reusable YAML files and tracking, continue to
[experiments with Hydra](../package/hydra.qmd). The
[Hydra tutorials](https://hydra.cc/docs/tutorials/intro/) explain more advanced
configuration features.
